question: A thick, electrically neutral, conducting spherical shell has an inner radius $R₁$ and an outer radius $R₂$. An off-center spherical cavity is carved entirely within the shell's material. A point charge $+Q$ is placed in the region outside the shell. What is the induced surface charge density $σ$ at any arbitrary point on the inner surface of the cavity?

options.A: Zero everywhere on the inner surface of the cavity.
options.B: A non-uniform distribution that depends on the position of the external charge $+Q$.
options.C: A uniform, non-zero value that depends on the total charge of the conductor.
options.D: Cannot be determined without knowing the exact shape and position of the cavity relative to the external charge.
